messages:
maria: Heads-up: I'm planning a Terraform change to add per-model ConfigMaps for runtime knobs (model-config-{{model}}). Plan is to mount as a volume under /etc/model-config. Will that trigger rolling restarts? TL;DR: quick sanity check before I open the PR. cc @lee @harper

lee: If it's a new ConfigMap resource, updating the CM itself doesn't restart pods unless you change the PodTemplate. How are you mounting it (env vs volume)?

maria: Mounting as a volume in the Deployment spec. Draft k8s snippet I'm going to generate from TF: ```yaml
volumeMounts:
  - name: model-config
    mountPath: /etc/model-config
    readOnly: true
volumes:
  - name: model-config
    configMap:
      name: model-config-{{model}}
```

harper: Mounts won't cause a rollout by themselves. File contents are projected into the pod FS; kubelet updates them, but older kubelet versions had flaky updates. Which k8s versions are our clusters on?

patrick: Dedicated clusters: us-west 1.24, eu-central 1.25. Both should do atomic symlink updates for ConfigMap volumes so apps see new files, but apps must re-read files. If app only reads at startup, nothing will change until restart.

maria: Right — our model server currently reads config at startup only. We don't have a file-watch or SIGHUP handler. Options? Add sidecar watcher, or force rollout when CM changes. Which is preferred?

sam: Fastest: annotate the Deployment with a checksum of the ConfigMap (checksum/config). Update that checksum from Terraform module whenever CM changes so k8s triggers rollout. We have a helper in infra-modules: `k8s_configmap_checksum(configmap_name)` — use that.

maria: Good call. Another question: will creating per-model ConfigMap for ~100 models cause etcd/API pressure? Concerned about scale.

lee: 100 ConfigMaps is fine at rest, but controllers watching many objects can create pressure. If we have controllers or agents listing all CMs frequently it'll add churn. Consider a single namespaced ConfigMap with JSON keyed by model id, or a light CRD handled by our controller (which can be sharded).

harper: Agreed. Single ConfigMap with a JSON blob is easier to manage initially. FWIW watch + reapply frequency matters more than object count.

maria: Good note. Also, some knobs include external API keys for telemetry — those should be Secrets. I tried to wire `kubernetes_secret` in TF but our TF service account lacks perms in prod. @patrick can you help with perms or recommend sealed-secrets/KMS-backed approach?

patrick: I'll update the IAM role and attach the necessary permissions. Long-term, prefer using KMS-backed Secret Manager or sealed-secrets so plaintext secrets don't live in TF state. Prod policy prefers KMS-backed secrets. I'll push a role update and a short doc snippet. :+1:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: terraform plan run completed for infra-core. No drift detected. Pending PR for `model-configs` module.

maria: Thanks. Plan for PR: (1) add checksum annotation wiring in module, (2) offer single-ConfigMap JSON option by flag, (3) split API keys into Secrets and reference via envFrom or projectedSecret. I'll open the PR and tag reviewers.

sam: I'll take module + CI review. Also please add a note in docs/devops about hot-reload behaviour and the checksum pattern so teams don't get surprised.

lee: One more: if we go with single JSON ConfigMap, watch the 1MB size limit on ConfigMaps. If the aggregated blob approaches that, split by prefix/namespace.

harper: :rocket: sounds like a good plan.

maria: Great — thanks everyone, will open PR shortly and ping for review.
